passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for year-end 2024 compared to year-end 2023 can be found in Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as filed with the SEC on February 11, 2025 (“2024 Form 10-K”). BUSINESS AND OVERVIEW Overview We are a worldwide franchisor, operator, and licensor of hotel, residential, timeshare, and other lodging properties under a portfolio of compelling brands at different price and service points. We discuss our operations in the following reportable business segments: (1) U.S. & Canada, (2) Europe, Middle East & Africa (“EMEA”), (3) Greater China, and (4) Asia Pacific excluding China (“APEC”). Our Caribbean & Latin America (“CALA”) operating segment does not meet the applicable accounting criteria for separate disclosure as a reportable business segment, and as such, we include its results in “Unallocated corporate and other.” Under our asset-light business model and consistent with our focus on franchising, management, and licensing, we own or lease very few of our lodging properties. Under our hotel franchising arrangements, we generally receive an initial application fee and continuing royalty fees, which are typically based on a percentage of room revenues, plus for certain brands, a percentage of food and beverage revenues. Terms of our management agreements vary, but we earn a management fee that is typically composed of a base management fee, which is a percentage of the revenues of the hotel, and an incentive management fee, which is based on the profits of the hotel. In many cases (particularly in our U.S. & Canada, Europe, and CALA regions), incentive management fees are subject to a specified owner return. We also have license and other agreements with third parties for certain offerings, such as for our timeshare properties, MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy, Design Hotels, and The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, under which we receive royalty and certain other fees. Additionally, we earn fees for other uses of our intellectual property, including primarily co-branded credit card fees, as well as residential branding fees and certain other licensing fees. Performance Measures We believe Revenue per Available Room (“RevPAR”), which we calculate by dividing property level room revenue by total rooms available for the period, is a meaningful indicator of our performance because it measures the period-over-period change in room revenues. RevPAR may not be comparable to similarly titled measures, such as revenues, and should not be viewed as necessarily correlating with our fee revenue. We also believe occupancy and average daily rate (“ADR”), which are components of calculating RevPAR, are meaningful indicators of our performance. Occupancy, which we calculate by dividing total rooms sold by total rooms available for the period, measures the utilization of a property’s available capacity. credit_strengths.text: The asset-light franchising and licensing model generates fee-based revenue with minimal owned real estate, and operating margin sits above the sector median, indicating pricing power and cost discipline across the global brand portfolio.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure and dividends combined, and free cash flow covers dividends several times over, so the recurring distribution is funded from internally generated cash rather than incremental borrowing.

key_risks.text: Shareholder distributions exceed operating cash flow and free cash flow, with buybacks alone surpassing operating cash flow; the shortfall is bridged by balance-sheet capacity, so returns are sensitive to any lodging demand downturn.

The debt note shows meaningful near-term maturities, including notes due within the coming year and a large commercial paper balance, so refinancing access and the revolving facility are critical to liquidity despite the modest tagged debt figure.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage exceeds one comfortably but sits below the sector median and eased year over year, reflecting a higher average cost of debt as older low-coupon notes mature and are replaced.

Gross leverage is far below the sector median and net leverage is negative on a cash-netted basis, consistent with a minimal indicative financial risk profile; the tagged debt line understates gross borrowings shown in the debt note.

overall_credit_view.text: The credit profile is anchored by fee-driven cash generation and a net cash position, with leverage well below the sector median; the indicative minimal risk profile reflects this, though it is not a rating and coverage trails peers.

The current ratio is below one and below the sector median, driven by large current liabilities including near-term maturities; liquidity relies on the revolving facility and continued market access rather than working capital cushion.

credit_strengths.text: 輕資產的特許經營及授權模式產生以費用為基礎的收入，自有房地產極少，而經營利潤率處於行業中位數以上，顯示全球品牌組合具備定價能力及成本紀律。
經營現金流足以舒適地覆蓋資本開支與股息之總和，而自由現金流覆蓋股息數倍，因此經常性分派乃由內部產生之現金撥付，而非來自增量借貸。

key_risks.text: 股東分派超過經營現金流及自由現金流，其中單是回購已超越經營現金流；缺口由資產負債表能力填補，因此回報對任何住宿需求下滑均屬敏感。
債務附註顯示有相當規模的短期到期債務，包括於來年內到期之票據及龐大的商業票據結餘，因此再融資渠道及循環融資額度對流動性至關重要，儘管標記債務數字溫和。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率舒適地超過一倍，但低於行業中位數，並按年有所緩和，反映隨著較舊的低票息票據到期並被取代，平均債務成本上升。
總槓桿遠低於行業中位數，而按現金淨額基準計算的淨槓桿為負數，與極低的指示性財務風險狀況一致；標記債務項目低估了債務附註所示之總借貸。

overall_credit_view.text: 信貸狀況以費用驅動的現金產生及淨現金狀況為錨，槓桿遠低於行業中位數；指示性極低風險狀況反映此點，惟此並非評級，且覆蓋率落後於同業。
流動比率低於一倍，並低於行業中位數，乃由包括短期到期債務在內的大型流動負債所驅動；流動性依賴循環融資額度及持續的市場准入，而非營運資金緩衝。
